prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (capacity changes correlated with active Airport Capacity Plan and AAR at allocation); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline); Airport CDM Portal (shows data owners); Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger (AEL); Time Synchronization Service; Alert Distribution Hub; Performance Analytics Warehouse (PAW; aggregates compliance by carrier, route group, regulation, airport configuration, time band; no sensitive detail beyond authorized roles); Collaborative Decision Log (CDL); Business Rules Registry (BRR); Tower Sequence Manager and Ramp Movement Board (send actual movement milestones); Surface Surveillance Adapter (surface evidence retained for disputes/audit); Contingency Operations Console; North/South Runway. Silverpine (alias, element unspecified) SHALL accept emergency access only after IAS records incident reference and expiry. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity allows, frozen at horizon. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State (Airport Duty Manager (ADM) declares after consulting Regional Flow Manager (RFM), Tower Supervisor, System Support Engineer (SSE)): Slot Coordinator manual slots at console; DMS MUST NOT overwrite; role separation kept; reconnection reconciles into CDL; PAW gets outage record. Emergency access only ERC, ADM, SSE; audited; post-review by Data Governance Steward (DGS). Dual control for Ground Delay Program/AAR/Tactical Regulation Proposal changes. AEL logs access, config, exports, slot compliance events, time source. Compliance compares CTT, TOBT, actual times vs BRR tolerance; Slot Compliance State: compliant/early/late/exempted/substituted/cancelled/pending review. CDL keeps reason/time/flight per change; substitution records kept. Freeze-horizon changes need reason code, visible to RFM. RFM uses Post Operations Report to attribute noncompliance (operator, airport, airspace, weather, system); ADM reviews multi-flight late airport changes; findings adjust tolerances/reason codes/training under change control. DGS verifies audit fields complete/immutable, maintains ownership register via

New part:
S819: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall own operational weather classification inputs accepted by the Weather Ingest Gateway.
S820: The Airline Operations Coordinator shall be accountable for airline-supplied schedule intent, readiness status, and Target Off Block Time updates submitted through approved interfaces.
S821: Each owned data element shall have a defined business meaning, allowed value range, update authority, retention class, and escalation contact.
S822: Freshness indicators shall be displayed on the Common Situation Display wherever stale data could affect sequencing, metering, regulation, or resource allocation decisions.
S823: The freshness indicator shall include the time of last accepted update, the maximum permitted age, and a visual state that distinguishes current, aging, stale, and unavailable data.
S824: The Time Synchronization Service shall provide the common time basis used for freshness calculations across the Regional Flow Platform.
S825: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, and Departure Metering Service shall reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp.
S826: Validation rules shall include schema checks, mandatory field checks, code set checks, temporal sequence checks, and operational plausibility checks.
S827: The Flight Data Exchange shall validate Flight Intent Message content before the data is made available for operational use.
S828: The Surface Surveillance Adapter shall apply position quality checks and shall mark uncertain observations before they are used by surface decision functions.
S829: The Airline Interface Adapter shall apply carrier-specific format checks while preserving the common operational meaning required by the Regional Flow Platform.
S830: The Handling Resource Planner shall validate resource quantities, task timing, and allocation identifiers against active operational reference data.
S831: The Business Rules Registry shall hold the current validation thresholds, allowable reason codes, and exception rules approved for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, and Contingency Fallback State.
S832: When a discrepancy is detected, the affected component shall mark the data as disputed and shall preserve the prior accepted value until an authorized correction is available.
S833: The Data Governance Steward shall coordinate discrepancy resolution with the responsible operational owner and shall record the disposition in the Audit Event Ledger.
S834: Urgent discrepancies that could change a metering, arrival regulation, or slot allocation decision shall be raised through the Alert Distribution Hub and reviewed in the Digital Briefing Room.
S835: The System Support Engineer shall investigate technical causes of missing, delayed, duplicated, or transformed records and shall provide evidence needed for stewardship decisions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
